name: Prose
summary: The text styles every block uses, from display headline to kicker, and an article's readable body.

guidance.useFor: Long-form text (an article, a case study) in .lue-prose, and the look of headings and short text anywhere: lue-display for a hero, lue-title for an article, lue-h2 and lue-h3 for sections and cards, lue-lede and lue-dek for the sentence under a headline, lue-kicker for a label above one.
insteadUse: Choosing a heading's level: the document outline decides it; the class only sets the look
Text that has to stand out as a warning: Alert
content: One h1 per page; don't skip levels to get a smaller heading - use the class
Keep kickers to a few words: they are read before the heading
Ledes are one or two sentences

rungReason: Classes on native headings, paragraphs and lists: the semantics are the elements', the look is CSS.

a11y.role: None of its own: the elements keep theirs
a11y.name: n/a

keyboard.action: Passes over it: nothing here takes focus

rules: Sizes grow with the viewport between fixed limits, and stay in rem so text zoom scales them (WCAG 1.4.4)
Muted text (lede, dek, kicker, excerpt) keeps 4.5:1 on every surface
Kickers are upper case by CSS only, so screen readers read the words as written
